comparison: Strong agreement on methodological development (C2, C27-C48). Both evaluations find the C-MAP protocol modifications well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes technical specifications and measurements, while peer reviewers highlight the substantial improvement over current standards and rapid data acquisition capabilities. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on segmentation pipeline capabilities (C50-C51, C56). Both evaluations support the methodology, though OpenEval notes limited validation details while peer reviewers praise the quantification capabilities. Reviewer 1 noted uncertainty about sub-cellular resolution performance, which aligns with OpenEval's observation of limited validation details.

Partial overlap on experimental scope (C3, C32-C33, C54-C55). OpenEval groups sample size and marker coverage claims together, while peer review combines these with segmentation methodology. Both find the approach well-supported, with OpenEval noting the lack of quantitative validation for 'most neurons' claim.

Agreement on validation findings (C57-C59, C62, C158). Both evaluations treat axon tracing results as confirmatory of prior observations. Peer reviewers explicitly note these findings validate the techniques, while OpenEval emphasizes corroboration with citations and new single-axon tracing validation.

Strong agreement on morphometric analyses (C64-C69). Both find quantitative homeostasis data convincing. OpenEval notes the flexible regulation interpretation is supported but mechanisms unexplored, while peer reviewers emphasize consistency with previous reports and comprehensive single-cell analysis.

Agreement on neuron scaling observations (C70-C78). Both evaluations support the quantitative data showing size-dependent differences. OpenEval explicitly flags allometric growth and fission threshold explanations as speculative, while peer reviewers focus on the convincing quantitative evidence without challenging interpretations.

Agreement on neuron type-specific dynamics (C79-C85). Both find the differential regional and cell-type patterns well-supported. OpenEval notes distinct regulatory mechanisms are inferred but not tested, while peer reviewers emphasize the comprehensive single-cell level analysis across large sample sizes.

Strong agreement on regeneration time course (C86-C97). Both evaluations support the biphasic pattern and differential dynamics across neuron types. OpenEval emphasizes the substantial sample size (251 samples) and validation of prior observations, while peer reviewers note the convincing data and confirmation of previous results.

Agreement on region-specific regeneration dynamics (C98-C103). Both find the differential growth rates and temporal correlations well-supported. OpenEval notes coordinated reconstruction interpretation lacks direct mechanistic links, while peer reviewers treat the comprehensive analysis as validating the techniques.

Agreement on comparative regeneration analysis (C104-C107). Both evaluations support the statistical validation of prior models with enhanced resolution. OpenEval emphasizes single-cell resolution and larger sample sizes, while peer reviewers focus on confirmation of previous results through comprehensive analysis.

Agreement on muscle architecture validation (C108-C114, C110-C112). Both find the regional muscle characterization well-supported. OpenEval notes appropriate acknowledgment of antibody limitations (C122-C123), while peer reviewers highlight the differences in body wall muscle patterns as a strength.

Agreement on muscle connectivity observations (C115-C121, C120-C121). Both evaluations support the high-resolution structural findings. OpenEval notes interconnected musculature interpretation lacks functional validation, while peer reviewers acknowledge these as new observations demonstrating technique utility.

Strong agreement on β-catenin-1 RNAi effects (C124-C129, C127-C128). Both find the regional muscle differences and RNAi phenotype convincing. OpenEval notes correlation with A-P polarity lacks established causality, while peer reviewers specifically highlight this as a new observation linking muscle pattern to body axis patterning.

Agreement on glial and neuronal associations with muscle (C130-C133, C165). Both evaluations support these observations. OpenEval notes functional significance not directly tested, while peer reviewers acknowledge the detailed cellular interactions as demonstrating the potential of the approach.

Agreement on muscle-neuron spatial-temporal relationships (C134-C137). Both find the close proximity observations and correlation interpretation supported. OpenEval notes directional relationship not established, while peer reviewers acknowledge the observations as new findings without challenging the correlation interpretation.

Agreement on inr-1 RNAi phenotypes (C139-C147, C139-C151). Both evaluations support the multiple phenotypic observations. OpenEval notes the interpretation linking changes to locomotion defects is correlative, while peer reviewers specifically highlight reduced glial projections as a strength and new observation.

Agreement on differential inr-1 effects (C148-C151). Both find the preserved neuron-muscle versus disrupted glial-muscle connections well-supported. OpenEval notes mechanistic uncertainty acknowledged by authors, while peer reviewers treat the glial projection reduction as a convincing new finding.

Both rate as UNCERTAIN regarding muscle scaffold hypothesis (C34-C35, C165-C166). OpenEval flags the guidance role as speculative without functional perturbation experiments, while peer reviewers note uncertainty about sub-cellular resolution performance needed to establish scaffolding relationships. Both acknowledge spatial correlations but question mechanistic inference.

Agreement on methodological advantages (C153-C155). Both evaluations support the claimed improvements over confocal microscopy. OpenEval notes lack of direct quantitative comparisons makes some claims qualitative, while peer reviewers emphasize the substantial improvement and rapid data acquisition as demonstrated strengths.

Agreement on sub-cellular resolution limitations (C159). Both acknowledge this constraint. OpenEval notes appropriate acknowledgment of limitations in the manuscript, while peer reviewers (Reviewer 1) directly raised concerns about unclear performance at sub-cellular resolutions based on shown data.

OpenEval R20 summarizes major findings including growth patterns (C160-C164), while peer R4 focuses specifically on neuron scaling quantitative data. Both support the growth pattern findings, with OpenEval noting the fission correlation (C163) is highly speculative without direct experimental evidence.

Minimal overlap on validation context. OpenEval R6 addresses neuron scaling with statistical analysis (C70-C78), while peer R3 broadly acknowledges confirmatory findings (C4) as validating the methodology. Both treat validation positively but focus on different aspects.

Minimal overlap. OpenEval R11 addresses muscle architecture validation including antibody limitations (C108-C114, C122-C123), while peer R3 broadly notes confirmatory findings (C109) validate the techniques. Both are supportive but address different scopes.

Partial overlap on regional muscle differences. OpenEval R13 focuses on β-catenin-1 RNAi validation (C124-C129), while peer R6 emphasizes anterior-posterior muscle pattern differences (C125-C126) as demonstrating technique utility. Both are supportive.

Minimal overlap. OpenEval R13 addresses muscle architecture differences validated by prior work (C124), while peer R3 broadly treats confirmatory findings as validation. Both supportive but different focus.

Partial overlap on methodology advantages. OpenEval R19 emphasizes speed and throughput claims (C153-C157), while peer R2 focuses on segmentation and quantification capabilities (C156-C157). Both are supportive of the methodological improvements.
